newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X reports progress in Jakarta gold talks.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X reports progress in Jakarta gold talks.

text.p: The head of Canadian mining company Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Monday the firm was making progress in talks with its local partners over the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province.
"We are continuing negotiations with our Indonesian partners," David Walsh, Bre-X chairman and chief executive officer, told Reuters in Jakarta.
"We are doing our best to be able to satisfy the requirements of the government. We're making progress," he said.
Walsh said last Thursday he expected an agreement this week.

He said the Indonesian government had given Bre-X and Barrick Cold Corp until February 14 to reach an agreement with their respective local partners over the Busang find before the go-ahead for further development.
Bre-X estimates there are at least 57 million ounces of gold at Busang currently worth over $21 billion.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to team up with Barrick, and the Mines and Energy Ministry said in December they had agreed to split Busang, with 22.5 percent going to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick and the remainder to the government.

Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80-percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 pecent each by timber tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought 50-percent shareholdings in two companies with minority stakes in two of the Busang areas.
State tin miner PT Tambang Timah, meanwhile, said on Monday it had entered into "serious" negotiations with Hasan over an equity participation in Busang.

"We are now in a serious talk with PT Askatindo and PT Amsya Lina over Timah's interest in Busang. The results (of the talks) are so far very satisfying," corporate secretary Prasetyo B. Saksono told Reuters.
Saksono said Timah, also listed in London, had in late January expressed an interest to having a five to 20 percent stake in Busang.
Saksono declined to give further details over the talks with Hasan, who chairs the Nusamba Group, saying it had not signed any agreement.
The other 50 percent of Askatindo and Amsya Lyna are controlled by the family of Indonesian businessman Syakerani.
